    The deck weight character (a lemma of an earlier draft) #

    An earlier draft of the manuscript (lem:deck-weight-character, not in the current revision): "Define the character of a closed walk in K to be the element of L = Hom_ℤ(H_ℤ, ℤ) sending an integer ray weight h to the weight of the walk under a mesh-weight lift of h; by Lemma 7.4 this does not depend on the lift. A closed walk whose lift joins X̃ to gX̃ has character −θ_g."

    Formalization. The deck group is the fundamental group of the coned complex at the basepoint (Deck), so a closed walk is a deck element g and its weight under a mesh weight W is the transport potW of the edge weights along g (MeshWt.walkWt). The deck class θ_g is ζ(g o₀) − ζ(o₀) for the object values ζ of the universal ray weight on the lifted projective category (Proposition 7.2(2)), defined for g in the stabilizer H of the base component (the deviation of Proposition 7.2(1)). Deviation: with the orientation conventions of the formalization (arrows of A₀ go along paths, rv is the weight of the path) the identity reads walkWt g = h(θ_g) (walkWt_eq), the sign of the source coming from its opposite convention for object values (−b_x at P_x).

      The deck weight character (an earlier draft's lemma): the weight of a closed walk g in the stabilizer of the base component under any mesh-weight lift W of an integer ray weight h is h(θ_g), where θ_g = ζ(g o₀) − ζ(o₀) is the deck class of Proposition 7.2(1).
